## Objective
Make agent subprocess termination reliable across all three adapters (claude, codex, pi): children run in their own session/process group, group kill is checked, and the port is closed on every exit path including raises in on_event.

## Design summary
- Session leadership: spawn the external CLI through a portable exec-wrapper `python3 -c "import os,sys; os.setsid(); os.execvp(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[1:])" -- <original argv>` (macOS ships no setsid binary; python3 is probed at /opt/homebrew/bin/python3). Implement once in a shared helper module and use it from all three adapters - divergence between adapters is the disease this ticket treats.
- Kill: target the process group (`kill -- -<os_pid>` semantics are now valid because the child is a group leader). Check the kill result; log and surface failures instead of ignoring them.
- Port close: wrap event handling so a raise in on_event cannot skip safe_port_close - use try/after (or rescue + re-raise after closing). Apply on all exit paths.
- Known sites to fix: elixir/lib/rondo/claude/cli.ex lines ~83-87 and ~283, elixir/lib/rondo/codex/cli.ex line ~237, elixir/lib/rondo/pi/cli.ex line ~232.
- Test-first order per the ticket: (1) repro test that leaves an orphaned grandchild with current code (assert process liveness after kill), (2) the fix, (3) raise-in-on_event test asserting the port closes. Cover all three adapters.

## File scope
Include: elixir/lib/rondo/{claude,codex,pi}/cli.ex, their test files, plus ONE new shared spawn helper module (none exists today - verified). Exclude: adapter consolidation (RON-141), any other behavior.

## Constraints
Must work on macOS (BSD userland) and Linux. If platform behavior is ambiguous, stop and pause - do not invent behavior. No remote writes; local commits only.

## Verification
